attempts.note: A lightweight symmetric above-deck Warren truss with strengthened central bottom chord and compression-governed diagonals sized for weak steel and the full moving-load envelope.
Attempt 1 is a Warren truss with 4.0 m depth: bottom chord on the deck, top chord at mid-panel nodes, and diagonals throughout, all sized for the 236 kN vehicle plus dead load.

Same Warren layout as attempt 1, re-sized by force: tension diagonals and the two midspan diagonals drop from CHS139.7x6.3 to CHS114.3x5, end chords and end bottom chords are lightened, and the high-force chords stay at CHS168.3x6.3.

Attempt 2's Warren layout with the top chord raised from 4.0 m to 4.2 m, which lowers chord forces about 5% and keeps every member's utilisation below about 0.75 at the weakest steel; section sizes are otherwise unchanged.
Attempt 2's Warren layout, with the lightly loaded end bottom chords cut to CHS76.1x4 and the bottom chords D2-D3 and D4-D5 dropped to CHS139.7x6.3; diagonals and top chords are unchanged.
Attempt 4's Warren layout and section sizes with the top chord lowered from 4.0 m to 3.8 m, shortening the diagonals to save mass while keeping chord utilisation near 0.75 at the weakest steel.

Attempt 5's Warren geometry at 3.8 m depth, with top chords T2-T3 and T5-T6 reduced to CHS139.7x6.3 (about 0.67 utilisation) and bottom chord D5-D6 reduced to CHS114.3x5 (about 0.78 at nominal steel), trimming about 60 kg while keeping every member's utilisation below about 0.8 at nominal steel.

Attempt 6's Warren layout with the top chord lowered from 3.8 m to 3.7 m to shorten the 14 diagonals by about 0.1 m each; section sizes are unchanged, so chord utilisation rises about 3% to roughly 0.83 at nominal steel.
Final attempt: resubmitting attempt 7's verified Warren truss (top chord at 3.7 m, unchanged sections) because it is the lightest design with margin at the weakest steel.
